what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/walk-through-an-app-like-its-users: walking an app's journeys in a real browser on the person's own computer and reporting what to fix, and mapping an app's screens and controls to write journeys from.

payload.label: Walk through an app like its users
payload.job: Check that people can still do what they come to my app for after a change: walk each journey in a real browser, keep pictures, a log and a video, and tell my coding agent exactly what to fix, then check the fix
payload.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer (so it reaches local, VPN and Tailscale addresses the computer reaches) and walks each journey in a browser context of its own. A journey is DATA: { id, goal, expect_every_step?, steps: [{ id, intent, do?, expect? }] }. `do` is one action a person takes: goto { url }, click { target }, fill { target, value }, press { key }, upload { target, files } (files relative to fixtures_folder) or wait { ms }; a target names a control as a person sees it: { role, name } or { role, name_contains }, with nth when several match. `expect` lists what must then be true: text_visible, text_absent, url_contains, title_contains { text }; control_present, control_absent { target }; field_value { target, equals }; checked { target, equals }; no_console_errors; no_failed_requests. A step with no `do` (or a learned action whose control has gone) stops as needs_decision with the actions the page offers, as `do` objects to copy back; the AI chooses one and runs again with it in `learned` or in the journey. Answers the report: verdict, each step with its pictures (the touched control boxed and numbered), console errors and failed requests, `fixes` (for each failed step: what was expected, what was there, the steps that reproduce it and the evidence), `decisions_needed`, `learned` (the actions that passed, to replay next time) and, given previous_report, `compared_with_previous` (fixed, still_failing, newly_failing, still_passing, now_passing). Every run walks every step again; nothing passes because it passed before. Evidence is written under evidence_folder (or a new folder in the computer's temporary folder) and report_file names the saved report.

app_url.description: Where every journey starts: an http, https, file or data address the person's computer can open.

goal.description: What the person on this journey wants done, in their words.

expect_every_step.description: Expectations added to every step, such as { "kind": "no_console_errors" }.

learned.description: Actions to take for steps whose journey gives none: a previous report's learned list, or a choice from decisions_needed.

previous_report.description: The report of an earlier run: its learned actions are replayed and every step is compared with it.

version.description: What build of the app this is (a commit, a preview name), kept in the report and every fix.

fixtures_folder.description: The folder upload files are named relative to.

evidence_folder.description: Where pictures, logs, videos and report.json are written.

devtools_address.description: A browser already listening, such as http://127.0.0.1:9222 from obscura serve or a Chrome started with --remote-debugging-port.

payload.label: Map an app's screens and controls
payload.job: Find the screens of my app and what a person can do on each, so journeys can be written to check it
payload.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer and follows its links within the same origin, at most most_screens screens (20 at most). For each screen: its address, title, headings, the same-origin links, every visible control with its role and accessible name, the actions it offers as `do` objects ready to paste into a journey for tool:walk-through-an-app-like-its-users, a picture, and the console errors and failed requests seen while it loaded. not_opened lists links that were found but not opened.

payload.label: Read what a running app really shows
payload.job: Drive my running app through some steps and report what is actually on the screen after each: which controls exist, what a click would land on, errors, timing
payload.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer, does each step's `do` (the same actions as a walk: goto, click, fill, press, upload, wait, on a control named by role and name), then reads what the page holds as the step's `observe` asks: `elements` (for each match of a selector: its box, cursor, stacking, opacity, whether it is disabled, what a pointer aimed at its own centre would land on, and `pointer_is_self`, which tells a control that is missing from one a layer covers), `count`, `attributes` (named attributes and the form value), `text`, `global_path` (whether a dotted name exists on the page and its kind) and `media_ready` (milliseconds until a video or audio can play). It asserts nothing and fails nothing: a step that cannot complete comes back with `completed: false` and `blocked_by`, its readings are still taken, and the run goes on. The page is never intercepted or stubbed; requests reach the real server. Page errors and failed requests are listed. Use tool:walk-through-an-app-like-its-users to check that people can do what they came for, with expectations and a verdict; use this to see why something is not working.

app_url.description: The address of the running app: http, https, file or data.

id.description: Unique within the list. Defaults to step-N.

do.description: One action: { action: goto, url } | { action: click, target } | { action: fill, target, value } | { action: press, key } | { action: upload, target, files } | { action: wait, ms }. A target is { role, name } or { role, name_contains }, optional nth.

observe.description: Readings to take after the step, each under a name you choose: { read: elements, selector, limit? } | { read: count, selector } | { read: attributes, selector, names: [attribute names], limit? } | { read: text, selector, most? } | { read: global_path, path } | { read: media_ready, selector, timeout_ms? }.

picture.description: Keep a picture of the page after this step.
